title: Café table from primitives
prompt: Write a Blender Python script that builds a café table scene: an espresso cup on a saucer, a spoon, sugar cubes and a croissant. Use only primitive meshes (cube, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus).

oldPrompts.prompt: Write a Blender Python script that builds a café table scene — an espresso cup on a saucer, a spoon, sugar cubes and a croissant — using only primitive meshes (cube, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus).
oldPrompts.why: A style pass reworded the case file and split one sentence into two, which turned a trailing "using only primitive meshes" into a standalone "Use only primitive meshes." The case file recorded the change on the day. This file did not, so for a day the site printed the new wording above two results that had been scored on the old one, and `primitives` is one of the scored checks. Nothing was re-scored: both results below stay on the wording they were given. Caught on 2026-09-21 by harness/check-prompts.mjs, which now diffs every published wording against the runs.

groundTruth: The render, and the script that made it: the objects a person would name unprompted, at sizes a person would accept. A 5 cm spoon and an 11 cm croissant are checkable in the source.

checks.label: All five objects
checks.how: Table, cup on saucer, spoon, sugar cubes, croissant. All five present in the scene.
checks.rule: Pass if all five can be pointed at in the render as separate objects. One missing, or hidden behind another, fails it.

checks.label: Primitives only
checks.how: Every mesh comes from a primitive_*_add call, as the prompt requires.

checks.label: Spoon reads as a spoon
checks.how: A bowl and a handle on one axis, recognisable in the render.
checks.rule: Pass if the spoon is one connected piece with a bowl at one end, wider than the handle, and the handle running from it in a line. Loose parts, or no handle, fail it.

checks.label: Croissant reads as a croissant
checks.how: Recognisable in the render without the filename.
checks.rule: Pass if it is a crescent that is thickest in the middle and tapers to both tips, with segments or scoring across it. A smooth curved tube fails it, and so does a segmented one with no taper.

checks.label: Consistent scale
checks.how: Object dimensions in the script compared against each other and against life.

harder: Ask for the croissant's layered curl specifically, which is what the primitive set makes hard.
